Register an exact R type for an Arrow type

Source: R/registry.R
arrow_register.Rd

A typed package, such as 'zuint', 'decimal' or 'zutempo', tells zuarrow which R class is the exact form of an Arrow type. It does so in its .onLoad(), when zuarrow is installed; the registration lasts for the session and is removed when that package unloads.

Usage

arrow_register(
  key,
  to = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  package = NULL,
  exact = TRUE
)

arrow_unregister(key)

arrow_registry()

Arguments

key

A format string, a prefix pattern or an extension name.

to

NULL, or a function of (array, schema) or (array, schema, lossy) returning an R vector.

from

NULL, or a function of (x) returning an array handle.

class

The R classes from handles.

package

The registering package, so its registrations are removed when it unloads.

exact

Whether the conversion is exact.

Value

arrow_register() and arrow_unregister() return key invisibly. arrow_registry() returns a data frame with columns key, kind, class, package and exact.

Details

The key is one of:

  • an Arrow format string, matched exactly: "l" for int64;

  • a prefix pattern ending in * for parameterised types: "d:*" for every decimal, "tsn:*" for every nanosecond timestamp;

  • an extension name, such as "r.decimal".

When several keys match a column, the extension name wins, then the exact format string, then the pattern registered first. So a decimal128(38, 0) column is read by a "d:*" registration, even where it holds integers; naming a prototype of another registered class in the to of arrow_to_r() is how a caller opts into that class's handler instead. A package that registers a pattern again, as on a reload, keeps its place among the patterns; arrow_unregister() forgets it.

to converts Arrow to R: a function of (array, schema), the column's array and schema handles, returning an R vector of the array's length. It may be implemented in C against nanoarrow's r.h layout. It is called once per batch, and the pieces are combined with c(). A function of (array, schema, lossy) also receives the caller's lossy policy, so a handler can apply it to values its class cannot hold, such as one equal to its NA sentinel: an error under "error", NA with a warning under "warn". A to that cannot be called with two or three arguments is a zuarrow_registry_error.

from converts R to Arrow: a function of (x) returning an array handle of x's length, used for every object that inherits from class. It receives the whole column, and the column's type is that array's, in arrow_schema() too. An array of another length is a zuarrow_registry_error. Where several registrations' classes match an object, the one whose class comes first in class(x) is used, for from and for a prototype in the to of arrow_to_r().

Inside to, arrow_to_r() on the same column uses the built-in conversion, so a handler can start from it.

A registration declares whether it is exact. One that is not is used only under lossy = "warn" or "allow", and may not replace a type whose built-in conversion is exact. An extension is exact when its storage type is: an inexact registration for arrow.bool8, arrow.json or arrow.uuid is refused, and one that would read a column of exact storage is a zuarrow_registry_error. Registering a key again replaces the earlier registration, with a message naming both packages when another package owned it.

A dictionary or run-end encoded column is matched by its value type, not its index or run-end type, and to receives an array of its decoded values, one per row. Values of a fixed width, binary or string decode; any other layout is a zuarrow_type_error.

Registered handlers apply to the top-level columns of a data frame and to the fields of nested data frames, at any depth, not to the items of a list column. A field under a null row of its data frame is NA.

Examples

arrow_register(
  "l",
  to = function(array, schema) arrow_to_r(array, to = character()),
  exact = TRUE
)
arrow_registry()
#>   key   kind class package exact
#> 1   l format          <NA>  TRUE
arrow_unregister("l")
